newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross appeals for food aid for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross appeals for food aid for North Korea.

text.p: The world Red Cross body IFRC described the food situation in flood-hit North Korea as critical on Monday and called for urgent aid.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said it had raised less than a fifth of a $18 million emergency appeal for North Korea it launched in November.
North Korea, suffering acute food shortages it blames on devastating floods in 1995 and 1996, said on Monday that it had only half the grain needed to feed its people.
IFRC spokesman Jon Valfells said the Geneva-based agency was able to raise only enough funds for food shipments month by month.
The last IFRC shipment of 1,800 tonnes of maize and rice would reach North Korea shortly and the next one in about a month.
"We're managing to hang on by the skin of our teeth," Valfells said.
On Monday, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said North Korea's 24 million people were suffering "temporary food problems".
Valfells said: "We don't hear of people dying of starvation. But we see signs of malnutrition. The situation is alarming and critical."
Last week, the IFRC said that food rations in North Korea had dropped to a level four times lower than normally considered essential for a healthy population.

In January, Washington gave permission to Minneapolis-based Cargill Inc., the world's largest private grain trading company, to export 500,000 tonnes of wheat and/or rice to North Korea in what was expected to be a barter arrangement.
